newsitem.title: VATICAN: Pope, German bishops discuss abortion counselling.
newsitem.headline: Pope, German bishops discuss abortion counselling.

text.p: Pope John Paul and Germany's bishops on Tuesday discussed the role the Catholic Church should play in counselling services for women seeking abortions.

The Vatican said the Pope met the German prelates at their request "to discuss and explore in an in-depth way how Catholic family counsellors can be correctly involved" in services required by law in Germany.
According to German law, a woman who wants an abortion has to discuss her decision first with a counselling service. She can have the abortion afterwards if she wishes.
The Catholic Church in Germany has been split over the issue.
Some bishops say the Church should have no part in a process that could eventually lead to abortion, which the Roman Catholic Church considers murder.
Other bishops say the Church should take the opportunity to to explain to a woman the alternatives to abortion, such as adoption.
A Vatican statement said no decision was taken at the meeting.
"The exchange of opinions took place in a fraternal climate and the decisions to adopt will be indicated after a careful evaluation of the results of the meeting," the statement said.
It said all participants at the meeting recognised that the issue was "of great importance not only to the Church and society in Germany but also in many other countries."
"The question concerns the concrete application of the doctrine of the Church in the current situation, in the context of a pluralistic society," it said.
It said the German bishops proclaimed their adherence to the Pope's 1995 encyclical "The Gospel of Life".
That encyclical branded abortion and euthanasia as evils no human law could justify.

Participants at the meeting included Cardinal Joseph Ratzinger, the German head of the Vatican's powerful Congregation for the Doctrine of the Faith, and Cardinal Angelo Sodano, the Pope's Secretary of State.
